answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the range read as a modern outdoor clay range, a military training facility, or something stylized?
answers.answer: Make it a modern outdoor clay shooting range.

answers.ask: Does a round end on a score target, a time limit, or a number of missed targets?
answers.answer: Use a short time limit for each round, with the score based on how many clay pigeons the player shoots.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D first-person clay shooting map set at a modern outdoor clay range. A fixed central shooting station overlooks open range ground, with clay-pigeon launchers positioned at varied points around the station so targets can fly in from multiple unpredictable directions; keep clear sightlines and open sky above the range.
agent_notes: A shooting range with no opposing team and no route through it is the one thing Aim Trainer is for, and range-directed is its shape: a firing line, a target field in front of it, and safe ground behind. The launchers positioned all over fold into target-practice, bent from graded downrange plates to clay traps sited around the range so clays arrive from unpredictable directions rather than one lane; station-loadout stays as the gun rack behind the line. The player stands in one place and never walks, which is the gallery-shooter case stage B answers with SET - the range is still fully built, but nothing has to be reachable, so traversal and jump-gap checks are skipped and the route stays on the proven P0 pipeline. Decided without a user: a modern outdoor range dressed with a skyline of open sky and low buildings, one bounded range rather than several stations as separate maps, and the timed round with its per-clay score is scripting rather than geometry, so no capture or objective zone was placed.
